\section{Retarded function}
For the retarded function the convergence factor is $\eta>0$, and for real $\omega$
\begin{equation}
\int_0^{\infty} dt\, e^{(i\omega-\eta)t} = \frac{1}{\eta-i\omega} .
\label{eq:ret}
\end{equation}
\section{Advanced function}
For the advanced function the sign of the convergence factor is reversed, $\eta<0$, and we find
\begin{equation}
\int_0^{\infty} dt\, e^{(i\omega-\eta)t} = \frac{1}{\eta-i\omega} .
\label{eq:adv}
\end{equation}
